$3\tan\left(\frac12x\right)=-2, so \tan\left(\frac12x\right)=-\frac23$ — M1

$\frac12x=-0.588\ldots$ — M1

Inverse tangent.

$x=-1.2$ — A1

No extra values in the stated domain.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$\frac{y+2}{3}=\tan\left(\frac12x\right)$ — M1

$Attempts to isolate \tan(\frac12x).$

$f^{-1}(x)=2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x+2}{3}\right)$ — M1 A1

Inverse tangent then multiply by $2$; must be a function of $x$.

Lower endpoint $-5$ — B1

Upper endpoint $1$ — B1

[5]
